item.title: Anthropic targets $90 billion IPO at $1.4 trillion valuation
item.description: Anthropic PBC is preparing for an initial public offering aiming for a fully diluted valuation of $1.4 trillion. The company plans to raise up to $90.4 billion, including a private placement with major investors. It has reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion, showcasing significant growth in recent months. The IPO is scheduled to price on November 18 and begin trading the next day.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: New York: Anthropic PBC is seeking a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, in a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public.The Claude chatbot maker and its co-founders are seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement. The base offering would raise up to $64.4 billion, with shares marketed for $70 to $78 each, according to a filing on Tuesday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Anthropic is offering 801.4 million shares, while backers are selling 23.6 million shares.The figure also includes a private placement set to raise $26 billion in aggregate, to Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Broadcom Inc., Alphabet Inc.'s Google, Micron Technology Inc., Microsoft Corp., Nvidia Corp. and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., the filing shows.135721915At the top of the price range, Anthropic would have a market value of about $1 trillion, based on the shares outstanding listed in the filing. Accounting for employee stock options, restricted shares and stock reserved for the company's charitable donation matching program, Anthropic would have a fully diluted value of about $1.4 trillion.Read more: Microsoft market cap beats Nvidia's for first time since June 2025Anthropic's ambitious target, including the private placement, would hit roughly $100 billion when including a so-called over-allotment option or greenshoe, Bloomberg News calculations show. That would top SpaceX's $75 billion base offering, or the $86.2 billion it raised with the greenshoe.The goal defies jitters from a sharp selloff in AI-related stocks last week, driven by expectations that politicians promising tougher regulation of data centers and related infrastructure will drive up costs and limit development of the technology.Investors are under pressure to decide whether valuations in AI reflect a plausible trajectory for a technology that many expect to transform the economy and society as a whole, or overconfidence in an investment theme that hasn't yet proven its staying power.Read more: Fed’s Christopher Waller opens door to 50-basis-point December rate hike after hot CPI The widespread adoption of Claude Code and rival tools by software developers point to the potential transformation of a wide range of professional activity, from discovering new miracle drugs to navigating complex legal and accounting rules to running a factory. Already, more than 90% of contributions to Anthropic's code base were written by Claude, the filing shows.Anthropic has introduced so-called vertical solutions in these areas, with particular emphasis on healthcare and life sciences. It counts Novartis AG Chief Executive Officer Vas Narasimhan as one of its board members. The company's seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, are offering 3.38 million shares each in the IPO, the filing shows. The IPO is set to price on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and trade the following day, according to terms of the deal reviewed Bloomberg.Sales are surging. The company reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, the filing shows. Anthropic had a $65 billion run rate figure at the end of July, Bloomberg News reported. Bloomberg

item.title: US stocks: US market falls as hot inflation, hawkish Fed fuel rate-hike fears
item.description: US stocks closed lower after hotter-than-expected inflation data strengthened expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike and raised the possibility of more aggressive tightening. Rising Treasury yields and weakness in technology stocks, particularly Nvidia, weighed on the market, while investors also assessed hawkish Fed comments and Anthropic’s upcoming IPO.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: US stocks closed lower on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected inflation data strengthened expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase in December and raised concerns that policymakers could tighten monetary policy more aggressively, Reuters reported.The Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, exceeding the 0.3% increase forecast by economists polled by Reuters. It marked the third consecutive monthly gain of at least 0.4%, following a 0.6% rise in September.The data came after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise short-term interest rates in December even if inflation had moderated. He added that policymakers should consider a larger, half-percentage-point increase if price pressures worsened.Markets are now fully pricing in a rate increase of at least 25 basis points at the Fed’s December meeting, according to CME FedWatch, up from an 84% probability on Monday. The odds of a 50-basis-point increase rose to 11.8% after receiving no consideration in the previous session.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe two-year US Treasury yield, which is particularly sensitive to expectations for Fed policy, surged nearly 20 basis points and was on track for its biggest one-day increase since April 9, 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced sweeping global tariffs.Treasury yields rose even as oil prices fell to two-month lows after US officials played down the prospect of imminent military action against Iran.“What kind of has the market spooked a little bit is this idea of, ‘Well, we were already pricing in a December hike ... but maybe it’s not 25, maybe it’s 50, and maybe the Fed’s more worried about inflation than I am, so let’s sell some stocks,’” said Jason Ware, chief investment officer at Albion Financial Group in Salt Lake City, Utah.“From our perch, that is irrational. The thing that has pushed CPI up over the last six months and has the Fed a little bit more concerned and therefore has restarted hiking rates is because we’ve seen oil, energy and diesel push through in terms of inflation. If we have oil now going the other way ... this is all going to settle down.”The S&P 500 fell 28.46 points, or 0.38%, to close at 7,521.48. The Nasdaq Composite declined 185.90 points, or 0.74%, to 25,067.23, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 161.95 points, or 0.31%, to end at 52,227.80.Technology stocks come under pressureThe S&P 500 and Nasdaq had advanced for two consecutive sessions, recovering from the previous week’s sharp losses triggered by concerns that tighter government regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout.Also Read: Wells Fargo upgrades US AI infrastructure stocks to neutral after chip routThe S&P 500 technology sector fell more than 1% on Tuesday, making it the worst performer among the index’s 11 major sectors.Nvidia dropped nearly 6%, extending its two-session decline to about 10%. The chipmaker’s shares have faced pressure amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang after the company launched an internal investigation into allegations involving a Chinese businesswoman.The Information reported allegations that Huang’s relationship with the executive facilitated the shipment of at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chips through Chinese companies.Losses in the broader Philadelphia Semiconductor Index were more limited following two consecutive sessions of gains, highlighting continued volatility across the AI trade.Several Fed officials adopted a hawkish tone on Tuesday.Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said the central bank needed to deliver at least two more quarter-point rate increases to bring inflation down and might need to act quickly.Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said he believed the current policy rate remained “fairly accommodative.”Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman stopped short of calling for further rate increases but acknowledged that inflation remained the central bank’s top priority.Anthropic IPO draws investor attentionInvestors are also preparing for Anthropic’s expected stock-market listing later this month.The AI company said its initial public offering could raise as much as $64.4 billion and give it a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.4 trillion.Anthropic’s listing could intensify competition among major AI companies for investor capital and prompt portfolio repositioning.Neocloud company CoreWeave was scheduled to report quarterly results after Tuesday’s closing bell. Concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom and CoreWeave’s debt burden have weighed on its shares, which are down about 33% this year.CoreWeave and peer Nebius both ended the session lower.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Wells Fargo upgrades US AI infrastructure stocks to neutral after chip rout
item.description: Wells Fargo upgraded its outlook on US AI infrastructure stocks to neutral from negative, citing improved valuations after a steep semiconductor sell-off. However, it warned that slowing AI investment and rising depreciation costs could pressure earnings in 2028.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Wells Fargo upgraded its view on US artificial intelligence infrastructure companies to “neutral” from “negative,” saying a sharp decline in semiconductor stocks had improved the sector’s risk-reward profile despite persistent concerns about slowing AI investment, Reuters reported.Semiconductor shares have fallen about 38% from their June highs, while valuation multiples have contracted significantly. The brokerage said current prices already reflect much of the expected slowdown in AI-related earnings growth.Also read: Traders raise odds of 50 bps Fed rate hike as CPI rise exceeds expectations“Risk-reward is reasonable,” analysts led by Ohsung Kwon said in a note on Monday.Current semiconductor valuations imply annual earnings growth of roughly 8%, according to Wells Fargo.Democratic victories in last week’s US midterm elections, including in states where opposition to new data centres has increased, fuelled concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout. The resulting sell-off erased about $3 trillion from the market value of S&P 500 companies.However, Wells Fargo warned that markets have not fully priced in the risk of an earnings downturn in 2028 as capital spending peaks, supply increases and depreciation costs rise.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe brokerage estimates that AI-related investment added about eight percentage points to S&P 500 earnings growth over the past year.“The tailwind is expected to continue in 2027,” the analysts said, but it could largely disappear in 2028 as spending growth slows and depreciation expenses increase.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
